### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **214** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **154** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **154**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **99** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ab42fa612464d2a1a09e78c8ab2c62d73c23255c` — the merge of head `84e3f0ab42caded742dda94aa315d7148dc815da` into base `28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ab42fa612464d2a1a09e78c8ab2c62d73c23255c && git checkout ab42fa612464d2a1a09e78c8ab2c62d73c23255c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c 84e3f0ab42caded742dda94aa315d7148dc815da && git checkout -B drift-repro 28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c && git merge --no-ff 84e3f0ab42caded742dda94aa315d7148dc815da

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 28ef35e0e3799e1305e82c2d12f0515ca6bf519c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** at head `84e3f0ab` · `Implemented-by:` `claude/issue-28591-rehydrate-connectors` · `Reviewed-by:` this seat (lane ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`). `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. No `packages/spec` file is touched and no accept set changes, so no `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is owed.

| Check | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #28591` is the only closing keyword. One `@objectstack/service-automation` patch changeset. |
| Scope | 5 files, +434/−0. Not governed. Region-local to `service-automation/src/plugin.ts`: a `kernel:bootstrapped` hook re-reads the declaration and runs one `fatal: false` reconcile, only when the fingerprint of the enabled provider-bound entries differs from the last reconcile's. `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` is untouched. |
| Measurement first | At `d94dd3a6`, after a restart the package was listed and its flow served, but its connector was absent from `GET /automation/connectors`. Flows survive a restart through automation's own `kernel:ready` sync; the fix takes the same consumer-side route for connectors, at a hook that does not depend on plugin order. |
| Evidence | Permanent dogfood case `install-local-restart-connectors.dogfood.test.ts`: 1 failed at BASE, 5 passed after. Unit `connector-boot-registered-reconcile.test.ts`: 4 cases, among them a plain boot with exactly one reconcile (control) and an unknown-provider entry that is logged and skipped with the boot completing. One ablation turns exactly the 3 second-reconcile cases red. The whole service-automation suite passes: 251 files, 3177 tests. |
| Gates | CI on the head: 50 check-runs, 38 success, 12 skipped, none red. `check-expected-skips --pr 28639`: OK. Mergeable `clean`. |
| Accepted deviation | One row added to `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (Failure modes), outside the claimed surface: that table said every configuration fault outside a reload is a hard boot error, and that is no longer true for an installed package's entry at a restart. |

**Noted, not filed (agreed):** the flows of an installed package survive a restart only because install-local's `kernel:ready` handler runs before automation's flow sync, an order nothing declares. This is an inference from reading the code; no reach was measured under `os serve`.
**Order with PR #28587** (in the merge queue, same file, different region): whichever lands second goes through the queue against the new base.

**Landing:** not governed. The seat lands it now (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`).
